subject: Security Exhibit — audit rights, retention & redaction guidance
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acme-bio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit — scope clarifications, retention & redaction

Marcus — thanks for the call this morning. Before we move the Order Form + exhibit to our procurement team I need to lock down two items that our legal/compliance team flagged: 

1) Evidence retention & redaction: Acme needs assurance that any customer-provided test evidence that contains PHI/PII will be redacted before being stored in Redwood's shared evidence repo. Can you confirm whether redaction occurs on your side or if we need to submit a redacted extract? Also: what is Redwood's retention window for submitted artifacts (logs, pen-test reports, snapshots)?

2) Pen test / inspection windows: we want a short, defined staging window (maximum 5 business days) and explicit notice periods. We also need to understand the rollback/backup criteria if a test impacts our staging environment.

We tried to capture this in a short checklist — attaching our procurement checklist. If you can propose concrete exhibit language or a short playbook that maps to our checklist, legal can move faster.

Appreciate a clear one-page summary and a proposed clause (or a redline) we can attach to the Order Form.

Thanks,
Sophie Martin
Sr. Security Program Manager
Acme Biotech
attachments: acme-procurement-checklist.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acme-bio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — scope clarifications, retention & redaction

Sophie — thanks for the clear checklist (and good questions). I pulled together a short playbook and proposed exhibit text that directly maps to your items. Key points up-front: 

- Redaction: Redwood will accept original evidence from customers but will apply automated PII/PHI redaction on ingestion followed by a legal-team manual spot-check for high-sensitivity artifacts. If you prefer to submit already-redacted artifacts, we'll accept those and mark them 'customer redacted' in our evidence ledger.

- Retention: Default retention for submitted evidence is 180 days from ingestion. For regulated customers we offer S3 retention carveouts (e.g., 365 days) via Order Form option or can implement shorter retention windows on request. We'll include a retention toggle in the exhibit and a mechanism for customers to request early purge.

- Pen-test/staging windows: Standard default window is 3 business days. We can support up to 10 business days by mutual agreement for complex tests, but we will include a maximum 5-business-day default staging window in the exhibit for Acme as you requested. Notice: 72 hours notice for non-intrusive tests, 10 business days for intrusive testing requiring elevated access. Rollback criteria: Redwood's staging policy requires a snapshot and automated rollback point prior to any intrusive activity; if any test causes instability, Redwood will trigger the rollback and notify the customer within 2 hours.

I've attached: proposed-security-exhibit_v1.docx (full exhibit with toggles) and a short evidence-handbook.pdf that explains how artifacts are stored, redaction steps, and the manual review flow. Laura / Olga — please review the drafted clause for legal redlines and confirm whether we need additional attestation language for SOC 2 artifacts.

Next step: Sophie — if this maps to your checklist, can you confirm and we'll send a legal redline next (DocuSign/Order Form-ready)?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-security-exhibit_v1.docx; evidence-handbook.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acme-bio.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — scope clarifications, retention & redaction

Marcus / Sophie — quick legal redline & comments. Thank you Marcus for the clear options — below are the items we've redlined in the attached doc: 

- Evidence retention: Accepted 180-day default, but added an explicit customer-initiated purge workflow (48-hour SLA for purge confirmation) and a statement limiting Redwood's use of retained artifacts strictly to audit/evidence purposes.

- Redaction obligations: Added a mutual-cooperation clause — Redwood will perform automated redaction but customers must flag high-sensitivity artifacts before submission; Redwood will not be liable for undisclosed PHI submitted without notice. Also required an attestation checkbox in the Order Form stating whether Acme will submit redacted or raw artifacts.

- Pen test windows & rollback: Tightened the notice language — 10 business days for intrusive tests requiring privileged access; 72-hour notice for non-privileged tests. We inserted a rollback SLA: Redwood will restore the prior snapshot within 4 hours of detecting a stability-impacting event. If restoration fails, escalation to an exec-level incident bridge will be triggered and remediation timelines will be negotiated in good faith.

- SOC 2 artifacts & attestations: Added language that SOC 2 reports and auditor correspondence are treated as "customer confidential evidence" and will be stored behind additional access controls; extraction of raw SOC 2 reports by Redwood is forbidden without a signed data-processing addendum.

I've attached redline-security-exhibit_v2.docx with inline edits. Sophie — if these look acceptable I'll prepare a final clean copy for the Order Form and a short one-page summary for procurement. Marcus — pls confirm you can support the 48-hour purge confirmation SLA operationally.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
attachments: redline-security-exhibit_v2.docx
